why_ai: Libraries are physical civic places with in-person programmes and physical collections, and communities keep funding them, though reference, cataloguing and selection work is screen-based and AI-exposed.
why_clarity: Cataloguing and circulation follow codified rules and repeat endlessly, but whether a collection serves its community is judged loosely and surfaces over years.
why_digital: Physical books, boxes and buildings alongside licensed digital content, run by local staff for residents who visit in person and fund the library through local taxes.

why_ai: Platform software is delivered remotely and AI-native competitors can erode it, but decade-long contracts, migrations and consortium decisions protect incumbents.
why_clarity: Platform functions are well specified and procured against RFP requirements, though each migration and configuration is a distinct project.
why_digital: Library data in, hosted software out, sold through RFPs with demos and references rather than in person.

why_ai: Entitlement and access management is rule-driven screen work that automation absorbs, with platform lock-in the main protection.
why_clarity: Whether a licensed title is correctly activated and accessible is objectively checkable across thousands of near-identical titles.
why_digital: Licences, title lists and usage in, hosted platform and access out, bought by RFP.

why_ai: Holds and circulation automate, but physical items still move between branches by van and consortia stick with systems that work.
why_clarity: A hold fills or it does not and the same transactions recur millions of times, with wait times measured daily.
why_digital: Catalogue and holds data drive physical delivery of items between branches, bought by consortia through RFPs.

why_ai: Licensing and lending are fully digital and forecastable, though selectors' reads of local demand and publisher relationships still matter.
why_clarity: Loans, holds and expiries are counted exactly for every title, but which licence decision was right is known only months later.
why_digital: Licences and lending data in, digital loans out through apps, bought from platform vendors online.

why_ai: Appraisal and arrangement need an archivist handling boxes and judging lasting value, with donor trust involved, though description and screening are increasingly automatable.
why_clarity: DACS and EAD codify the output, but appraisal and arrangement vary by archivist and their value shows when researchers use a collection years later.
why_digital: Physical boxes in, a mix of handling and screen work, finding aids and digital objects out, bought by institutions through grants.

why_ai: Fragile physical materials need careful handling and imaging on site, and local trust matters, but OCR and hosting automate.
why_clarity: Imaging and OCR follow published guidelines with measurable quality, repeated page after page.
why_digital: Bound newspapers, film and photographs in, scanning and screen work, online collections out, bought by small institutions with grants.

why_ai: Serving small libraries runs through state libraries and consortia whose consultants know each director personally, and demand for shared services will persist.
why_clarity: Back-office services repeat across many similar libraries, but their effect on a small community is loosely measured.
why_digital: Shared systems and services delivered remotely to libraries reached through state and regional relationships.

why_ai: Research and content management are screen work exposed to AI research tools, protected by trusted relationships with partners and accountability for content spend.
why_clarity: Usage, seats and charges are countable and renewals recur, though research quality itself is judged case by case.
why_digital: Licensed databases and usage logs in, research and spend reports out, bought by firms through internal relationships and vendor negotiations.

why_ai: Matching and loading existing records is rule-bound and highly automatable; only the physical labelling of shelf-ready items needs hands.
why_clarity: A record either matches the edition and passes validation or it does not, across millions of near-identical cases.
why_digital: Physical items and records in, mostly screen work, catalogue records and processed books out, bought from vendors remotely.

why_ai: Harvesting usage and modelling cancellations is screen work that automation absorbs, with negotiation judgement left to people.
why_clarity: Usage and cost per use are measurable and the same analysis recurs for every licence, though cancellation consequences show only afterwards.
why_digital: Usage reports and licences in, analysis out, bought remotely by libraries and consortia.

why_ai: Citation indexing and metrics are screen work, but editorial judgements about journals are consequential and the curated archive and brand are hard to replace.
why_clarity: Selection criteria are published and indexing repeats at scale, though the value of a metric is argued over for years.
why_digital: Published literature in, curated indexes and analytics out, sold online worldwide.

why_ai: Writing reviews is screen work that AI summaries threaten, though named reviewers and trusted outlets still carry weight with selectors.
why_clarity: Review quality is a matter of taste and outcomes are never formally checked, even though the same format repeats for thousands of titles.
why_digital: Books and galleys in, reviews written on screen and sold by subscription online.

why_ai: Collection analysis is data work, but the cooperative's network of member libraries and its union catalogue are durable and trusted.
why_clarity: Overlap and holdings analyses are well defined and repeat per library and consortium.
why_digital: Holdings and lending data in, analyses and services out, sold to members remotely.

why_ai: Subject indexing and abstracting are screen work that machine indexing and free discovery over open metadata erode, protected by thesauri and society brands.
why_clarity: Indexing follows controlled vocabularies and repeats for every article added, with indexer consistency checkable.
why_digital: Published literature in, indexed records out, sold online through database platforms.

why_ai: Survey and strategy research rests on trusted relationships with library leaders and judgement about institutions, though survey analysis automates.
why_clarity: Strategy advice has no agreed measure of success and its effect shows years later, even where survey methods are codified.
why_digital: Survey data and interviews in, reports out, sold through relationships and some site visits.

why_ai: Indexing and record matching are increasingly automated; the moat is record access deals and user trees rather than people.
why_clarity: Record indexing and matching repeat across billions of records with checkable accuracy.
why_digital: Physical and filmed records digitised into online subscriptions sold to consumers worldwide.

why_ai: Negotiation with publishers is adversarial and relationship-based, and members trust their consortium, though the analysis behind it automates.
why_clarity: Usage and price analyses are defined, but whether a deal was good is contested and known later.
why_digital: Usage and price data in, negotiated licences out, conducted through meetings with publishers and members.

why_ai: Analytics on platform data is screen work that AI features absorb.
why_clarity: Dashboards and benchmarks are well specified and refreshed routinely.
why_digital: Transaction data in, analytics features out, delivered inside hosted software.

why_ai: Statutory authority over records schedules and library funding cannot be delegated to AI, and archives handle physical records too.
why_clarity: Rules and schedules are codified and applied repeatedly, but whether appraisal kept the right records is known decades later.
why_digital: Records and statistics in, rules, appraisals and grants out, with no market choice of provider.

why_ai: Preservation storage and fixity checking are automated infrastructure, protected by institutions' trust in long-lived providers.
why_clarity: Fixity and format checks are exact and continuous.
why_digital: Files in, preserved files and reports out, delivered as a remote service.

why_ai: Handling fragile books and film needs people at scanners, but cataloguing output and OCR are automating fast.
why_clarity: Imaging and record specifications are exact and repeat page after page.
why_digital: Physical materials shipped in, images and records delivered digitally, bought by remote contract.

why_ai: A qualified appraiser must inspect the material and sign a valuation the IRS can challenge, and donors choose a trusted name.
why_clarity: Appraisal methods exist but values rest on judgement and comparable sales, and are tested only if challenged.
why_digital: Physical papers and books inspected in person, a signed report delivered, found through dealer and institutional networks.

why_ai: Collecting and publishing member statistics is routine data work that automation absorbs.
why_clarity: Survey definitions are fixed and the same counts recur every year.
why_digital: Member-reported data in, reports and dashboards out, all online.

why_ai: Patron segmentation and email marketing are commodity analytics that library platforms and AI tools absorb.
why_clarity: Segmentation and campaign metrics repeat across clients, though their effect on library use is loosely measured.
why_digital: Library and census data in, segments and campaigns out, sold remotely.
